items.text: Snowfield, Yakutsk
It's an ordinary morning in Lesnaya Forest, located in the coldest part of Yakutsk.
A branch from a nearby tree breaks under the weight of the snow, sending a cascade of glistening flakes to the ground.
A snowy owl turns its head, its large round eyes fixed on the figures in the snow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sofia!

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Shh!

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: You've found them.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The number of ovinniks in the area has reached the minimum viable population size you calculated.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: That was just a rough calculation. We didn't have enough data about them, so I used the data of a similar species. We'll need more information to run a more accurate calculation.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's already October. It's minus 30 degrees right now.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: *sigh*
Sofia blinks, her eyelashes coated with white frost.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Even if you can make a fire through arcane skills to keep us warm, all the roads are still blocked.
As she speaks, her eyes are fixed on the ovinniks playing in the snow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I think they'll survive until May.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: How long have we been here?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Three months.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: And in that time we've located their nests, investigated the surroundings, and had a model established. Thanks to your help, the project is progressing much faster than expected.
Startled by the sound, numerous birds take flight, and the ovinniks scramble back to their cave.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Who's sawing wood in this weather?

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: The local sawmill, of course.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Umm. Oh!
Having suddenly thought of a new idea, Windsong starts scribbling on her map.
The forest falls into silence again.
But the silence comes too suddenly; they are immediately alert.
Not far from them, behind a pile of snow-covered branches, the head of a white wolf emerges.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sofia, look.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Stay low.
The white wolf leaps over the wood pile. It is clearly starving. Each rib is visible beneath its fur.

items.speaker: The White Wolf
items.text: *growl*
It sniffs at the cave's opening, its tail gently brushing the ground.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's looking for food.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: It won't fit through the burrow's entrance.
They watch the white wolf in the distance, neither one daring to move.
The wolf continues to pace around the cave. It has caught the scent of the ovinniks within.
At its command, more wolves emerge through the snow.
They gather before the cave, and the white wolf starts digging.
The other wolves patrol the area, apparently looking for any other entrances to the burrow.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Don't.
She pushes Windsong back down.
The white wolf has already made a hole the size of its upper body.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: No.
Once again, she places her hand on Windsong's shoulder.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The wolves will get them!
A sudden commotion interrupts their hushed argument, an ovinnik dashes out of the burrow and springs onto the white wolf.

items.speaker: Ovinnik
items.text: *roar*
The white wolf howls in rage. It dives to avoid the hit and bites the ovinnik on the shoulder. The two roll over in the snow.
More wolves circle around, pushing and nipping at the ovinnik. Soon enough, it is dripping with blood.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We can't just stay back and watch this happen!
Before Sofia can react, Windsong jumps up and charges toward the wolf pack.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Природа это числа и черты.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: You're not helping, you know.
Sofia has also rushed over.
She walks straight past Windsong, kneels before the wounded ovinnik, and checks on its injuries.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I didn't harm any of the wolves.
The worried look on Sofia's face makes her a little uneasy.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: We should head back. We really shouldn't leave any human scent here.
Coo-coo?
They follow the gentle cooing to the burrow. A fluffy head pops out from the hole dug by the white wolf.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Is that a cub?

items.speaker: Ovinnik Cub
items.text: Coo?
Enraptured, Windsong turns to Sofia, only to find tears in her eyes.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Stop here.
She catches Windsong's coat, stopping her from moving any further.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: We can't go any closer. We mustn't cross the line.
Frightened by her gaze, the cub quickly dives back into the burrow and vanishes from their sight.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Shall we go?

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Mm-hm.
She nods, casting one last glance at the burrow.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Let's go home.
Forest Cabin, Yakutsk
The cabin is warm and quiet. Only the crackling of the fire and the sound of Windsong's scribbling fill the air.
There is also the occasional sound of Sofia flipping through papers.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sofia, do we have any bear grease left? My fingers are horribly itchy.
Still caught up in the excitement of learning about the cub, she draws a tiny ovinnik on the map right next to where they found it.
Sofia puts down the papers and fetches her a jar of white salve.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Don't you arcanists have some kind of magic ointment? You know, ones that heal frostbite and such within seconds?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hm, probably, but I don't know much about them, to be honest. Sometimes, human medicines are more effective.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Can't ley lines make frostbite disappear?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: No. They can't change a fact.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Then you really shouldn't have taken your gloves off out there.
She takes some grease from the jar and starts slathering it on the back of Windsong's frostbitten hands.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha. Still trying to master the art of sketching with my gloves on. And let's face it, if we hadn't written down all the information on the spot, we'd still be clueless about their migration patterns.
She pushes a sketch over to Sofia.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Here. This is the latest illustration depicting the ley energy of this group of ovinniks.
She takes out another piece of paper.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And this is the graph we drew three months ago.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As you can see, the population's significantly increased, and some of them have started breeding.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We've made pretty significant progress in maintaining this sanctuary, but there's still a lot to be done.
She points at the map but quickly pulls back her finger, realizing there is still grease on it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The spot over there—yes, that's the lumberyard. It used to be part of the conservation area, but apparently not anymore.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: How long has the sawmill been there?
Sofia puts the newspaper down on the table.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Umm. This newspaper's from last week. Where's the latest one?

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: You can't be serious, Comrade Ekaterina. The ranger only goes to town once a week for supplies. All the newspapers we have are a week old.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: We've been here for months. Did you seriously not notice all this time?
She looks at Windsong with a hint of confusion.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: You do seem to care very little about the outside world. You've barely mentioned it since we entered the forest.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ahem. I was totally caught up with those ovinniks, so—

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: They seem to be all you ever want to focus on.
Throughout this conversation, Windsong has been absent-mindedly drawing on the paper.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's already October, Sofia. How much longer do you plan to stay here?

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: My work here isn't done yet. With the rate of human expansion in the area, it won't be long before they encroach on ovinnik territory. If I leave now, I'm worried the ovinniks here will be left vulnerable.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: I'm planning to set up a new conservation area in the spring—in a place where they and humans won't get in each other's way.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Then I'll have to make sure they settle in well. So, that'll be about a year from now.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: What about you, Ekaterina?
Windsong rests her chin in her palm, falling silent.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hm. I'll have to go back to the institute once my paper's done.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: If it gets published, people will learn about the critters here, and maybe some will come lend a hand.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Just like they did in Taryga.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: That would be just the help I need.
She walks to the window and looks at the snow outside.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: The ranger told us we had to leave in two days. They're closing off the area for the winter.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Three months. I doubt much has changed back home.
Following Sofia's gaze, Windsong peers out the window and scans the distant mountains.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I wonder if it's already started snowing at the institute.
